newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks close mixed, seen recovering.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks close mixed, seen recovering.

text.p: Croatian stocks closed mixed in sluggish trade on Tuesday with Croatia Banka dominating the market and traders foresaw a recovery after last week's dip.
"This is probably the beginning of mild growth. We expect most prices to regain the ground they lost last week," Hrvoje Bujanovic of IB Austria told Reuters.
Croatia Banka was the most active stock with 5,471 shares sold. It ended at 173 kuna, up three kuna or 1.8 percent from last Wednesday, when it last traded.
Transactions consisted of large packages of up to 2,000 units though traders could not identify the reason for its sudden popularity.
"There are no fundamental reasons to point out, but its price usually holds around 175 kuna and it will probably stay there," Bujanovic said.
"This is very unusual," said Marijan Palic at Auctor brokerage. "Traders will certainly react in a few days."
Eight of 18 active issues rose, eight fell and two closed flat. Volume shrank to 12,977 from 15,804 units and turnover fell to 4.2 from 5.3 million kuna.
Bujanovic was optimistic about food processor Podravka which closed 11 kuna higher at 273 trading on a handsome volume of 1,643 units. It lost 18 kuna last Thursday.
"Podravka has improved after a nervousnes about it last week and we believe in further growth," he added.

Blue chips, drugs firm Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka ordinary stock, suffered mild corrections that traders ascribed to a recent fall in the dollar and declines on European bourses last week. Their prices were likely to folow general trends in world markets, traders said.
Pliva slipped 6.5 percent to 560 with 830 units sold and Zagrebacka fell 4.1 percent to 2,360 kuna on volume of 400.
Palic said he had expected a much bigger fall in prices because of the decline in the dollar, "but now this hasn't happened I am very optimistic," he added.
Three of four active hoteliers, trading on meagre volumes, were on the losing side and one was flat.
One broker described Arenaturist, unchanged at 130 kuna and selling 152 units, as underpriced and bound to grow soon.
The rest of the tourist sector was likely to move upward only at the end of August when the peak season ends, they said.
Top gainer was Rijecka Banka, rising 15 kuna or 11.1 percent to 150 kuna on volume of 100 shares.
Shipyard Viktor Lenac, losing 18 kuna or 11.6 percent to 137 kuna, led decliners. It sold 652 shares.
